Hi Samira — thanks for the clear repro and the screenshot, that helps.

Short answer: we’ve seen embedded webviews block the SSO redirect chain when third-party cookies or SameSite policies are enforced, which prevents the IdP handshake from completing. We’ll do a quick triage and propose a short-term workaround + timeline for a persistent fix.

Planned immediate steps (mutual action plan):
1) Can you try opening the invite in the device’s external browser (long-press the invite link in the app and choose "Open in Chrome") — you mentioned desktop copy/paste worked, this will validate mobile browser vs in-app webview.
2) Ben (cc'd) will run a trace on the invite link to see where the redirect stops and share any missing relay-state or cookie flags.
3) If webview is the blocker, we can: a) provide a short-term manual claim code for affected vendor users, or b) issue a new invite URL with a relay-state param that avoids cross-site cookie dependence.

Ben/Laura — can you pick this up? I put PO numbers in the thread so we know the business urgency. Samira, if you can add a test device token or share a screenshare window tomorrow at 9am PT, that helps.

Thanks, Chloe. Quick tech notes from triage:

What I verified:
- H/T to Samira: when opened inside an embedded webview that suppresses third-party cookies, the IdP (SAML/OIDC) sets a session cookie during the broker redirect and the client never returns it to our origin on the final redirect. That leaves our session creation incomplete and the UI throws a generic sign-in failure.
- Repro: I reproduced the failure using an Android WebView (system webview) and a custom rule that strips Set-Cookie headers.

Short-term workarounds (pick one):
- Option A (fast): Manually issue a one-time claim code for Northshore vendor users — they can paste it on the portal claim page and skip the full SSO flow.
- Option B (medium): Send a special invite URL with relay_state and a short-lived query token that the mobile app can open in an external browser automatically (we'll provide a deep link + fallback). This avoids reliance on third-party cookies.

Longer-term fix (engineering):
- Add a fallback in our invite acceptance endpoint: if the browser/user agent identifies an embedded webview and the IdP does not return a session cookie, we will accept the short-lived token and complete account claim server-side. ETA for an engineering patch: 7–10 business days once scoped.

I attached the auth trace I captured (auth_flow_trace_1123.txt) showing the redirect chain and cookie headers.

Checklist for Samira to help us triage faster:
- Confirm whether your app webview is intentionally blocking third-party cookies (some MDMs enforce this)
- If possible, share a screenshare tomorrow at 9am PT or a sample device ID we can test against

If you want Option A now, we can issue claim codes for the two vendor contacts and un-block the POs today.
